card.band: 8 h. Many modules (settings, helm invocation, client plumbing, cache, RBAC) give natural buckets. A frontier agent gets the core path in some trials and misses the scoping and caching buckets on average. A weaker model stops at a hard-coded lookup stub.
card.cheat: Returning an empty map for every lookup passes only the disabled cases. Hidden fixtures cover present, absent and denied objects, with names and namespaces randomised.
card.grading: Hidden Go tests through public repo-server APIs use a fake Kubernetes client and chart fixtures (lookup of present, absent and namespaced or cluster-scoped objects, denied access, cache key behaviour, disabled-by-default). The existing repo-server and util/helm suites are a regression gate. Reward is the fraction of cases passed.
card.reference: Our own implementation, expected 1500-2500 changed lines across the repo-server, helm util, settings and docs. The upstream proposal discussion gives the design but no merged code (not found).
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of argo-cd at the base commit. The agent implements the Helm 'lookup' template function for manifest generation: a cluster-reader abstraction in the repo-server, per-application opt-in setting, RBAC and project scoping of lookups, caching and invalidation keys, and a fake-cluster test mode. Delivered through the Go packages and config.

facts.claim: Argo CD issue #21745 'Helm lookup function support' exists, opened 2025-02-03, still open with labels enhancement and proposal:in-progress
Upstream proposal adds an opt-in --helm-server-dry-run flag or serverDryRun Application field, default false, running helm template with --dry-run=server using destination cluster credentials
No merged Argo CD code implements Helm lookup; the issue has no linked PR and no maintainer says it is implemented
Only related PR is #27650 (warnings for helm lookup and docs), which is open and labelled Stale, with no lookup implementation

Maintainer crenshaw-dev is sceptical of lookup support and requires the proposal to detail how users scope lookup access per Application or AppProject (Oct 2025); he supports only docs and UI warnings (Apr 2026)
Argo CD is Apache-2.0 (Apache License 2.0, copyright The Argo Authors)
Seed's per-application opt-in setting and cluster-reader abstraction have fixed public names in any upstream design
Reference implementation of the seed's full scope (1500-2500 lines) exists outside our own work
Helm lookup does not work under helm template, which Argo CD uses for rendering (root cause)

v1.kill_reason: No strong reference obtainable. Upstream has no merged code and the maintainer has not accepted a lookup design. The seed's hidden tests depend on unpinned setting names, cluster-reader API and RBAC model, so a different valid design would fail, breaking the acceptance gate. Revive by re-seeding with a pinned public interface and fixed RBAC model, or a smaller scope such as core lookup plus disabled-by-default.

Band.why: No dated public evidence; at most 3 without it. The seed's 8 h band understates the scope.

Build.why: Estimated 3-4 days to build the reference and fixtures.

Fit.why: Go unit tests with fake clients fit gVisor; large module build is the risk.

Hor.why: 1500-2500 lines across repo-server, helm, settings, RBAC, caching and docs.

Multi.why: Natural buckets: core lookup, opt-in, scoping, caching, denial, cluster-scoped.

Real.why: Real repo at pinned release and a real open issue; but no merged code and a contested design.

Ref.why: No upstream reference; ours would be bespoke, and its interface is unpinned in the seed.

Seal.why: Reference is ours and not public; design is public in outline, so recall is a Band question, not a Seal one.

Surf.why: Fake-client fixtures give a sizeable but hand-written surface; no generator.

spike_plan.kill_if: Base suites are red or non-deterministic, the offline build needs network, or the fake-client harness cannot reproduce lookup results.
spike_plan.pass_if: Base build and existing suites run offline in under 30 minutes with deterministic per-test results, and the lookup stub shows the expected present/absent split in fake-client tests.
steps: In a networked throwaway Linux container, clone argoproj/argo-cd at 5f6569ec and run go mod download to fill the module cache.
Time go build ./cmd/... and go test ./util/helm/... ./reposerver/... at base; record green or red per test.
Using the vendored Helm version, run helm template on a chart with a lookup call and confirm lookup returns empty under template, and differs with --dry-run=server against a fake cluster.

Write a stub cluster-reader with a fixed interface and a serverDryRun-style setting, then render present, absent and denied objects with fake clients to check the test harness is deterministic across three runs.
Check that an empty-map stub passes only the disabled cases, so the grading split is real.

v1.summary: The seed's issue is real and open, with no merged lookup code upstream (only docs-level PR #27650), and Apache-2.0 is confirmed. It fails as written because the hidden-test interface is not pinned, so no reference can be shown to define the ceiling for other valid designs (K5); the smoke build is absent ({}), so build cost is unverified.
